# Ink recipes

## Iron gall

1. Crush 40 g of oak galls and soak them in 500 ml of rain water.
2. After a week, strain and add 20 g of iron sulphate.
3. Stir in 15 g of gum arabic, dissolved first in a little warm water.

> Iron gall ink is acidic. It eats steel nibs slowly and paper very slowly.

## Carbon

| Ingredient | Amount | Note |
| ---------- | -----: | ---- |
| Lamp black | 10 g | the finer the better |
| Gum arabic | 5 g | binder |
| Water | 100 ml | distilled |
| Clove oil | 2 drops | keeps mould away |

Grind the lamp black with the gum on a glass slab for **twenty minutes**,
then thin with water until it flows from a dip pen.

## Walnut

Boil green walnut husks for an hour, strain through a cloth and reduce by
half. Add a pinch of salt and a spoon of vinegar to fix the colour.

```text
husks   500 g
water   1 l
salt    a pinch
vinegar 1 tbsp
```

## Testing a batch

- Write the alphabet three times.
- Wait a minute, then drag a finger across it.
- Wet a corner and watch whether it runs.
- Note the result in the [field notes](Field%20notes.md).

## Safety

Iron sulphate is an irritant; wear gloves. Lamp black gets everywhere;
wear an apron. Walnut stains hands for a week; wear both.

## Storage

Keep inks in glass, out of the sun, and label every jar with the date.
Iron gall darkens in the bottle over months; carbon settles and needs a
shake; walnut grows mould unless salted.

Last line of the recipes.
